h1: I Built This LIC Surrender Value Calculator to Give You the Unvarnished Truth (2025)
description: Thinking about surrendering your LIC policy? It's a tough spot to be in, and I get it. Before you make a move, let's figure out exactly what you'd get back. I've built this free LIC Surrender Value Calculator to give you an honest, instant estimate. We'll break down the difference between the Guaranteed Value (GSV) and the more realistic Special Value (SSV), so you can make a decision with your eyes wide open.

content.text: Let's cut through the jargon. The 'surrender value' is the cash amount LIC gives you if you decide to end your policy before its official end date. To be eligible for any payout at all, you generally need to have paid premiums for at least two or three full years. If you're considering surrender because of low returns, check our LIC maturity calculator to understand what you'd receive if you let the policy run its full term. There are two numbers you need to know:

items: Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV): Think of this as the absolute minimum, legally guaranteed amount you'll get back. It's calculated based on a fixed formula from LIC's rulebook.

Special Surrender Value (SSV): This is the number that really matters. It's a higher, non-guaranteed value that LIC calculates based on their business performance and other factors. In almost all cases, the SSV is what you'll actually receive, and it's always equal to or higher than the GSV.

content.title: Step 1: Calculate Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV)
content.text: First, we calculate the absolute minimum you're entitled to. The formula is: (Total Premiums Paid Ã— GSV Premium Factor) + (Accrued Bonuses Ã— GSV Bonus Factor). These 'factors' are percentages defined by LIC that increase the longer you've held the policy.

content.title: Step 2: Estimate Special Surrender Value (SSV)
content.text: This is the more realistic, higher value. It's estimated with the formula: (Paid-up Value + Accrued Bonuses) Ã— SSV Factor. The 'Paid-up Value' is a reduced Sum Assured based on premiums you've paid. The 'SSV Factor' is LIC's internal multiplier. Since it's not public, our calculator uses a robust heuristic to estimate this value, giving you a much closer idea of your actual payout.

sections.title: The Big Question: Surrender vs. Make It 'Paid-Up'?

content.text: Before you surrender, you need to know about its smarter cousin: the 'Paid-Up' option. They are not the same, and choosing correctly can save you from a huge financial mistake. Compare your policy options using our Jeevan Anand, Jeevan Labh, and Jeevan Umang calculators to explore better policy alternatives.

items: Surrendering: You terminate the policy completely. You get a one-time cash payment (the surrender value), but you lose your life insurance cover forever.

Making it Paid-Up: If you can't afford premiums anymore (after 2-3 years), you can just stop paying. The policy doesn't die. It continues with a reduced Sum Assured. You won't pay any more premiums, and you'll still get this reduced amount at the original maturity date.

sections.title: My Advice: Smarter Alternatives to Surrendering Your Policy

content.text: I always say surrendering should be your absolute last resort. Before taking any drastic steps, check our loan optimizer to explore borrowing options and our retirement corpus calculator for comprehensive financial planning. Here are three things I'd consider first:

items: Take a Loan Against the Policy: If you need money for a short-term emergency, this is your best bet. You get liquidity (up to 90% of the surrender value) without losing your life cover. Use our loan optimizer to compare borrowing options.

Make it Paid-Up: As we discussed above, if you can't afford the premiums, just stop paying. Your policy stays alive with reduced benefits, which is far better than getting a pittance back and losing your cover.

The 'Buy Term, Invest the Rest' Strategy: If your issue is the low returns, explore our mutual fund screener and mutual fund overlap calculator for high-return investment options. Compare with our FD vs PPF calculator to see what matches your goals.

content.title: My Honest Advice
content.text: If you don't need the cash urgently, making the policy 'Paid-Up' is almost always the better financial move. You keep some life cover and your money continues to grow. Only surrender if you have a dire, immediate cash need that you can't solve any other way.

sections.title: The Official Process: How to Surrender Your LIC Policy

content.text: If you've weighed everything and decided to proceed, here is the step-by-step process you'll need to follow:

items: Confirm Eligibility: Make sure you've paid premiums for at least two or three full years, as required by your policy.
Gather Your Documents: You'll need the Original Policy Bond (this is crucial), a filled Surrender Form No. 5074, a copy of your PAN and Aadhaar, and a cancelled cheque for the bank transfer.
Visit Your Servicing Branch: The policyholder must physically go to the LIC branch that manages their policy to submit the surrender request.
Verification & Payout: LIC will verify the documents and process your request. The surrender value is typically credited to your bank account via NEFT within 7-10 working days.

sections.title: Your Questions, Answered: LIC Surrender Value FAQs

items.q: How do I calculate the surrender value of my LIC policy?
items.a: The simplest way is to use our calculator above. Just enter your policy details to get an instant estimate. The formula is a percentage of premiums paid plus a portion of your accrued bonuses, which our tool calculates for you.

items.q: After how many years can I surrender an LIC policy?
items.a: Generally, you can surrender a policy only after you've paid premiums for at least two or three full years. Some single premium policies may be surrendered after one year. Before this period, the policy has no surrender value.

items.q: Is the surrender value of an LIC policy taxable?
items.a: If you surrender after 5 full premium-paying years, the amount is generally tax-free under Section 10(10D). If you surrender before 5 years, the amount can become taxable, and any tax deductions you claimed under 80C can be reversed. Use our tax regime calculator to understand the tax implications for your specific situation.

items.q: How much money will I get if I surrender my LIC policy?
items.a: It's a percentage of what you've paid, and it starts very low. For example, after 3 years, you might only get back ~30% of your premiums. The value increases the longer you hold the policy. Use our calculator above to get a personalized estimate for your policy.

items.q: What is the difference between guaranteed and special surrender value?
items.a: Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) is the legally mandated minimum payout based on a formula of premiums paid. Special Surrender Value (SSV) is a higher, non-guaranteed amount that includes a portion of your bonuses. LIC will always pay whichever amount is higher.

items.q: Should I surrender my LIC policy or make it paid-up?
items.a: If you don't need cash immediately, making the policy 'Paid-Up' is almost always better. You stop paying premiums but keep a reduced life cover and get a payout at maturity. Use our LIC maturity calculator to see what you'd get at the end of the policy term. For overall financial planning, check our retirement corpus calculator. Surrender only for a dire cash emergency.

items.q: Can I surrender my LIC policy online?
items.a: As of now, the final surrender process is offline. You must visit your servicing LIC branch with the original documents to complete the process, though some initial forms may be downloadable online.

items.q: What documents are required to surrender an LIC policy?
items.a: You will need the Original Policy Bond, the filled Surrender Form (Form 5074), a copy of your PAN and Aadhaar cards, and a cancelled cheque for your bank details.

items.q: How long does it take to receive the surrender value amount?
items.a: Once your documents are submitted and approved, it typically takes 5-10 working days for LIC to credit the amount to your bank account.

items.q: Can a surrendered LIC policy be revived?
items.a: No, once you surrender and take the money, the policy is terminated permanently and cannot be revived. You would have to buy a new policy if needed.

items.q: Do term insurance policies have a surrender value?
items.a: Generally no, pure term insurance plans are for risk cover only and do not have a savings component, so they do not offer a payout on cancellation.

items.q: Will I get my bonus if I surrender the policy?
items.a: Yes, a portion of your accrued bonuses is typically factored into the Special Surrender Value (SSV). So, if your policy has earned bonuses, your surrender payout will be higher than the basic guaranteed value. Use our LIC maturity calculator to see how these bonuses grow if you let the policy run full term. Loyalty additions, however, are usually forfeited if the policy does not run its full term.
